messages:
Ivy: quick flag  I noticed multiple examples use different param names: `input`, `prompt`, and `prompt_text`. This is confusing for users. Proposing we converge on a single canonical API param and update snippets.
Ravi: Agreed. Can we pick a name that's explicit and cross-surface? `user_input` or `text_input`?
Priya: prefer `user_input` because it maps cleanly to chat, generation, and embeddings. `text_input` feels too narrow for non-text payloads later.
Ben: +1 `user_input`. We should add a short migration note and automated snippet test to catch regressions.
Ivy: good. I'll open a PR to change code samples and add a migration paragraph. Also will put a small note in Console: keep label as "Prompt" but add a tooltip: "API param: user_input (previously prompt_text/prompt)" for one release.
Ravi: can docs team write a mini-glossary entry: "prompt vs instruction vs user_input" so writers have guidance when to use which term?
Priya: I'll draft the blurb. Proposed text: "user_input  the raw text provided by an end user; 'prompt' is a subset used for single-turn generation; 'instruction' implies an imperative-style prompt for instruct-tuned models."
Ben: also add migration snippets for JS and Python and run snippet-tests in CI. Example to include: ```js
// before
client.generate({ prompt_text: 'Write a haiku' })
// after
client.generate({ user_input: 'Write a haiku' })
```
DocsBot: CI queued for PR #2401  running link-check + snippet-tests.
Ivy: action items: Priya  glossary blurb + examples; Ravi  add release notes checklist and tag PMs; Ben  add snippet-tests and lint rules; Ivy  PR to update snippets and Console tooltip ticket. I'll merge after CI green. :thumbsup:
